subject: Kickoff: Project Vantage — JPEG encoder evaluation (mucped23)
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kicking off the mucped23 work (Apr 13 – Jul 27). We're running this internally under the codename Project Vantage — use it in doc titles and the chat channel (#proj-vantage) so the encoder vendors don't show up in search.

The asset: our open-source mucped23 IQA database — human perceptual evaluations of images compressed with MozJPEG, libjpeg-turbo, and the jpegli encoder, built on 49 512x512 source images drawn from the CID22 validation set. jpegli applies insights from the butteraugli and JPEG XL lines to squeeze more quality-per-byte out of plain JPEG, which every image-heavy surface we run still serves.

Product question, plainly: do we switch our serving stack's encoder, and at which quality settings? Serving costs say yes if perception says tie.

Milestones: mid-May — dataset + eval harness internalized; late June — encoder bake-off on our own image corpus; mid-July — recommendation to the serving org.

Staffing and compute by May 1?

Lucia
